This draw has no subject-topic labels yet, so the row has no topic cells; its use-case and language cells are measured on its own draw. A NEW ROW OF THE DECISIO FAMILY AND A SERVING-CONFIGURATION VARIANT OF A LIVE ROW: the weights tachara-ai/Decisio-12b-tuned-commit-think@e36aeb24 are the same weights as the live Decisio 12B tuned commit row (tachara-ai/Decisio-12b-tuned-commit@245e00dc): 16 of 20 files are identical by LFS sha256 or git blob oid and by sha256, including all six safetensors shards, the index, tokenizer, config and chat template; exactly 4 files differ (decision_config.json, README.md, NOTICE, SHA256SUMS). The behavioural difference is decision_config.json only: decisio 0.31.0 to 0.35.0, a think default {factor 0.495, budget 256, types [choice]}, over_limit truncate at 45,000 tokens, and the flavor name commit to commit-think. It is a separate row and replaces none of the live rows; nothing is inferred about the author's third same-weights repository (Decisio-12b-tuned-calibrated), which was not measured. The name is 'Jev-compatible' only: it is a Decisio model, not a Jev model. AUTHOR'S OWN SERVER on our rented hardware, run unmodified (see code_revision), no shim. NATIVE OUTPUTS: probabilities for choice, noul and score from the option-letter readout (one vLLM label-logprob readout, softmax over the label tokens) at the repository's shipped per-type temperatures (yes/no 3.314, score 2.1109, choice 2-10 options 2.1317, 11-26 options 1.8766, 27-255 options 1.7181). CONFIGURATION: the repository's shipped flavor 'commit-think', exactly as shipped; we measured no other flavor or setting and infer nothing about one. THINK PASS (author's feature, on by default in this flavor): a choice question of at most 16 options whose served first-read top probability is below 0.37125 (0.75 x 0.495) is read a second time after up to 256 greedy reasoning tokens; the two reads are mixed in log space and served at the same temperature. Noul and score never think and a cut state never thinks. OBSERVED: 36 of the 746 think-eligible choice decisions thought, 7,621 reasoning tokens in total, 19 of them stopped at the 256-token budget; no noul, score or cut decision thought. TRUNCATION (author's over-limit truncate): a state whose rendered text exceeds the cut room (45,000 tokens minus the longest plain user turn minus 32) is cut to its START at a whitespace boundary within 64 tokens, with no marker, and answered by the single read without thinking. Exactly the 5 pre-registered long items (76,554 to 81,413 tokens before the cut) were cut to 44,801 to 44,816 tokens; the observed cut set equals the counted set. Their answers rest on the first part of the state only. They are answered, not refused, and counted as answers. COMMIT RULE (a disclosed non-raw, item-blind output transform, in the same way as the DOPEST 0.801 floor): for yes/no questions, a temperature-scaled P(yes) strictly between 0.20 and 0.80 is reported at the nearer band edge, 0.80 if it is above 0.5, otherwise 0.20 (exactly 0.5 goes to 0.20). The argmax never changes; the Calibration axis includes the effect of this transform, and we did not measure a variant without it. LABEL-SHAPE RULES ON BY DEFAULT: hide_index_keys, describe_options and desnake_labels, which act on the shape of the labels of any request, never on item text, ids, gold labels or item lists (source review confirmed item-blind); the answer keys are always the request's own keys. The frozen offline layout counter recorded 746 describe_options, 375 noul_as_letters and 4 hide_index_keys applications across the 1,500 draw rows. TRAINING DATA (author statement, not independently verified): the model card says the training data is not disclosed, that no Decision Index or JevBench evaluation items were used in training or checkpoint selection, that the data was decontaminated against both boards' public test sets, and that official training splits of some public benchmarks were used under their licences. USAGE: cost is billed on the engine-processed input (chat template and system turn included), 844,031 tokens by an exact offline per-item recount; the server-native input usage, 727,045 tokens without template and system turn, equals our first-party count exactly. jeff_1_1_large.disclosure: First measurement of jgeuter/Jeff-1.1-Large, a Jev-compatible model. Jeff-1.0-Large, Jeff-1.1-Medium and Jeff-1.1-Qwen-4B are separate measured models; nothing is inferred between them. DRAW: measured on the 27 Oct 2026 regular draw (fresh sealed items; not yet equated to the reference scale, so its numbers are shown as published, offset 0). This draw has no subject-topic labels yet, so the row has no topic cells; its use-case and language cells are measured on its own draw. The author's own serving path ran unmodified with native choice, noul and score probabilities. The shipped configuration uses a one-pass decision head and limited generated reasoning read back into the answer: 186 decisions were reasoned, none dropped, and 1,314 were one-pass (21,830 reasoning tokens). Fast reasoning resolved to shared on this hardware (no room for a second copy of the weights); a card with room for a second copy could use the copy path, so this result is for this hardware. The settings target the published latency and cost caps: decision_seconds 8.5, max_share 0.45 and max_output_per_decision 35. The commitment band changes yes/no probabilities; Calibration includes its effect. No alternative configuration was measured. The card reports public-231 scores and separately held-out tuning data; the data used to tune the JevBench-specific settings are not identified. Training data are not identified beyond the card's description of CC BY-NC and research-only sources; the author states no JevBench items were used. Training examples and overlap with JevBench were not independently checked. Question-aware retrieval answered the 5 long items at at most 8,192 input tokens, selecting state passages matching the question in original order, with a start-of-state fallback. These answers use retrieved passages, not the whole state. All 1,500 requests returned HTTP 200 with answers, no refusals or errors; zero exceeded 10 s (maximum 8.319 s, under the author's own 8.5 s decision limit). Measured p50 0.106 s and p95 8.269 s; the reasoned decisions are the slow tail; the common self-hosted latency assumption is twice p50 plus 0.15 s. Native usage is 620,215 input and 21,830 output tokens. Ordinary input counts match the independent count on all 1,495 ordinary items; the 5 retrieval answers stay within 8,192 tokens. The server counts one-pass input only: an uncounted second-prefill estimate totals 199,718 tokens (88,572 generation-prefill plus 111,146 read-prefill), not measured natively and not priced. Native nonzero output is generated reasoning and is priced as reported. DETERMINISM (record-only): in the pre-sealed smoke, one repeated probe, a short score question that took the reasoning path, returned different probability vectors on its two repeats; no other probe differed, and the forced-reasoning process showed none. Weights carry non-commercial CC BY-NC-4.0 terms, the same terms as the Jeff-1.0-Large row; listed for evaluation only.
